B.source_sentence: Suppose SYM(A) is a group and SYM(B) is a 3-subnormal subgroup of SYM(A).

N.source_sentence: In symbols, if SYM(N) is normal in SYM(M), and SYM(N \le P \le M), the subnormal depth of SYM(P) in SYM(M) equals the subnormal depth of SYM(P/N) in SYM(M/N).

H.source_sentence: Let SYM(H) be a nontrivial 2-subnormal subgroup of SYM(G) that is not normal (existence of such a pair of SYM(H) and SYM(G) is guaranteed by Fact (1)).
Let SYM(H) be a nontrivial subgroup of a finite group SYM(G) that is a join of two 2-subnormal subgroups SYM(H_1,H_2) of SYM(G) but is not itself 2-subnormal (such subgroups exist, see Fact (2)).

H.meaning: H is defined as \langle H_1 , H_2 \rangle

A.source_sentence: Let SYM(A) be the wreath product of the group of prime order with SYM(G).
Let SYM(A) be the wreath product of the group of prime order with SYM(G).
Equivalently, SYM(A) is the semidirect product of the additive group of SYM(\mathbb{F}_p[G]) with SYM(G) acting by left multiplication.

A = \\mathbb{F}_p[G] \\rtimes G.meaning: A = \mathbb{F}_p[G] \rtimes G is a semidirect product
A = \\mathbb{F}_p[G] \\rtimes G.source_sentence: Equivalently, SYM(A = \mathbb{F}_p[G] \rtimes G) is the semidirect product of the additive group of SYM(\mathbb{F}_p[G]) with SYM(G) acting by left multiplication.

\\mathbb{F}_p[G] \\rtimes H.meaning: \mathbb{F}_p[G] \rtimes H is a unique largest 2-subnormal subgroup
\\mathbb{F}_p[G] \\rtimes H.source_sentence: Note that if there does exist a fastest ascending subnormal series, it must be the first, because SYM(\mathbb{F}_p[G] \rtimes H) is the unique largest 2-subnormal subgroup of SYM(A) that is in SYM(N_A(B)) (in fact, it is equal to the whole group SYM(N_A(B))) and the growth beyond that can be no faster than in the series, because of our assumption that SYM(H < K < G) is the fastest ascending subnormal series for SYM(H) as a 2-subnormal subgroup of SYM(G) (Facts (3) and (4) allow us to go back and forth modulo SYM(\mathbb{F}_p[G]) to make the translation).

C_1.meaning: C_1 is defined as \mathbb{F}_p[G] \rtimes H_1, C_2 = \mathbb{F}_p[G] \rtimes H_2
